title: CKCLoomAuthorityBoundaryAndFuturePublisherFixtures
clause: Lock CKC/Loom authority and navigation boundaries and prove future Tailor/Studio publisher compatibility with fixtures only.

current_source_discovery: Inspect accepted CKC, Loom, projection-registry and media authority contracts plus current Tailor/Studio stubs only for declared boundary expectations.
Discover the stable main's actual navigation registry and typed fixture conventions before naming publisher fixture APIs.
stop_conditions: MT-395 or MT-388 is not accepted.
Fixture work would implement Tailor/Studio product behavior.
Authority ownership cannot be stated for every sample source and projection field.

scope.summary: CKC is the character-domain authority in SurrealDB and navigation parent of future Tailor. Tailor retains authority over garment, pose/cloth and solver outputs; Studio retains authority over its future creative-production records. Loom receives typed projections/relations only. This MT proves that boundary with publisher fixtures, not features.
acceptance_criteria: A typed authority matrix assigns CKC character/sheet/moodboard/media fields, Loom projection fields, future Tailor domain/solver fields and future Studio domain fields to exactly one mutable owner.
Navigation registry declares CKC as the parent route for character-owned workflows and supports typed future child routes without moving Tailor domain/solver authority into CKC.

Tailor and Studio fixture publishers register with the generic Loom projection registry, publish sample typed records/relations and prove schema/version rejection without shipping runtime modules or UI features.
CKC moodboard and future specialized canvases retain separate authoritative layout identities while Loom renders explicit projections; regression proof prevents cross-canvas clobbering.
Source update/delete/revoke fixture events rebuild or hide Loom projections without permitting reverse domain mutation.
proof_targets: Validate the machine-readable field/command/navigation authority matrix with zero ambiguous owners.
Run typed Tailor and Studio publisher fixture compatibility/version/revoke tests against real SurrealDB.
Run CKC/Loom/specialized-canvas isolation and canonical navigation tests; source scan proves no Tailor/Studio feature implementation.

same_project_private_resource_cases: Parent navigation does not imply visibility into private child-domain resources.
derived_resource_non_widening_cases: Fixture and real projections preserve source-scope intersection.
revocation_and_context_switch_cases: Source revoke hides projections and invalidates owner navigation.
remote_saas_mcp_sync_cases: Future remote publishers must map identity and scope explicitly.
metadata_side_channel_cases: Owner module, child route, source type and projection status do not expose denied resources.

hbr_int_009_tier_obligations.evidence: publisher registration, projection, navigation, denial and revoke events
registry compatibility, owner ambiguity and route health
navigation/render recovery correlation for shipped CKC/Loom surfaces

risk_if_missed: Future Tailor and Studio work will either hard-code new Loom bridges or blur CKC, solver and projection authority before implementation begins.

risks: CKC parent navigation is misread as Tailor data ownership.
Specialized canvas shares mutable identity with Loom.
minimum_controls: Source scan forbidding future feature code.

research_provenance.selected_approach: CKC parent navigation with explicit domain ownership and generic typed fixture publishers for future Tailor/Studio compatibility.
